summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted for assistance with bowel preparation ahead of an EGD and colonoscopy due to dysphagia and a history of colonic polyps. During admission, she was found to have esophageal candidiasis on EGD, which was treated with fluconazole. Due to a known drug interaction, her tacrolimus dose was temporarily reduced in coordination with the transplant team. She also developed acute kidney injury and acute diastolic heart failure, likely due to dehydration from bowel prep and recent diuretic use, which improved with IV fluids and a dose of IV Lasix. Her Lasix dose was adjusted post-discharge. She remained stable, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with follow-up plans for medication monitoring and primary care.
